svg.title: Protected workspace lifecycle and recoverable all-backend retirement
svg.desc: Create makes a named owned immediate child, attach accepts an already owned marker, and select verifies an existing child. Authenticated backend registration is separate and may follow offline local creation. Root and default are always protected. A confirmed non-default remove or delete journals its intent before requesting retirement of every known backend binding. Each backend fences new admission, revokes sessions and drains associated work, including historical registrations. Pending, unreachable or uncertain outcomes preserve the journal and files. Remove from app keeps the folder. Delete invokes a guarded macOS Trash adapter only after all verified receipts, persisting an exact file reference before the effect and verifying that object inside Trash with the old entry absent. Uncertainty returns to recovery without recursive deletion or removal of a replacement object.
svg.text: LOCAL IDENTITY · REGISTRATION IS A SEPARATE OPERATION
Create: name-only; attach: matching owned marker
Select: verify existing child; reject external or unowned paths
Private root identity; never adopt a legacy layout
Persist exact request before HTTP; record only a validated receipt
Backend owns workstation / child / active binding and revisions
Registration never creates a remote filesystem folder
Keep known backend receipts and stable IDs; a rebind retains history and marks other children stale.
Unknown ensure / rebind outcomes must reconcile before removal. Refresh stale current bindings first.
Choose Remove from app or Delete
Drain associated work across old registrations
No shared-job cancellation or history rewrite
Fenced + sessions revoked + active work drained
Only authenticated proof advances local cleanup
Keep the journal and folder bytes
Never infer success from missing work or files
Persist exact reference before the OS effect
Check Trash identity and old entry absence
Never recursively delete or touch replacements. Real OS Trash / installed dual-Mac verification remains separate.
